issues.title: [ALL-1] Clone, run the skeleton on the fixture, sign off the contract
issues.body:
Everyone: `pip install -r requirements.txt`, `python -m patchpilot.ingest fixture`, `streamlit run app.py`, `python -m pytest -q`.
Read `config/project.json` and `docs/ANTIGRAVITY_PROMPT.md`. Create your branch (`p1-data`, `p2-scoring`, `p3-assistant`, `p4-app`).

**Done when:** app runs, tests pass, and you commented "contract OK" (or raised a change request) on this issue.

Contract: `config/project.json`. Edit only files you own. Keep `python -m pytest -q` green.

issues.title: [P1-1] NVD downloader (CVE, CVSS, CWE, CPE, fix links)
issues.body:
Implement `ingest.sync_nvd(conn, start, end)` against NVD API 2.0 (`https://services.nvd.nist.gov/rest/json/cves/2.0`) for CVEs **published 2024-01-01..2025-12-31**.
- Use `NVD_API_KEY`; paginate (`resultsPerPage=2000`, `startIndex`); the API caps date ranges at 120 days, so loop in windows. Exponential backoff on 403/429.
- Cache raw JSON in `data/raw/nvd/` so a re-run never re-downloads.
- Fill `cve` (cvss = CVSS v3.1, else v3.0, else NULL; cwe = first CWE), `cve_product` (vendor/product from CPE 2.3 criteria, lowercase, dedupe), `fix` (references tagged `Patch` or `Vendor Advisory`).
- Call `db.rebuild_fts(conn)` at the end.

**Done when:** a `python -m patchpilot.ingest nvd` style command (add it to `main()`) fills the DB; counts printed.

Contract: `config/project.json`. Edit only files you own. Keep `python -m pytest -q` green.

issues.title: [P1-2] CISA KEV + current EPSS loaders
issues.body:
Implement `ingest.sync_kev` (returns NEW cve_ids; KEV JSON `dateAdded`, `dueDate`) and `ingest.sync_epss` (current scores + percentile) from the URLs in `config/project.json`. **Verify the EPSS URL first** (see https://www.first.org/epss/data_stats); if it moved, update `project.json` and tell the team.
Restrict EPSS rows to CVEs present in `cve` to keep the DB small.

**Done when:** after P1-1, running KEV + EPSS sync makes `scoring.ranked_queue(conn)` return real rows.

**Depends on:** P1-1

issues.title: [P1-3] EPSS history files for the backtest
issues.body:
Implement `ingest.download_epss_history(dates)` saving dated daily EPSS files to `data/raw/epss/epss_scores-YYYY-MM-DD.csv.gz`. Cutoffs to fetch: **2025-01-01 and 2025-07-01** (adjust if files are unavailable; tell P2 immediately).
Write a tiny helper `ingest.load_epss_history(date) -> DataFrame[cve_id, score]` for P2.
KEV `date_added` must be stored for all KEV rows (P1-2) because the backtest labels depend on it.

issues.title: [P1-4] Build and commit the data snapshot + FTS index
issues.body:
Add `python -m patchpilot.ingest snapshot` that builds `data/patchpilot.db` end to end (NVD + KEV + EPSS + FTS). Commit the DB to `p1-data` and open a PR.

- Update `.env.example` so `DB_PATH=data/patchpilot.db` is the default, and in `.gitignore` leave the snapshot tracked.
- Post the row counts on this issue.

**Done when:** `DB_PATH=data/patchpilot.db streamlit run app.py` shows a real queue.

issues.title: [P2-3] Backtest dataset builder
issues.body:
Implement the design in the `patchpilot/backtest.py` docstring. Build the as-of-T table: candidates = CVEs published before T and not in KEV as of T; label = KEV `date_added` within `horizon_days` after T (default 180); features = CVSS + EPSS from the file dated T. Cutoffs: 2025-01-01 and 2025-07-01.
Guard against leakage: no KEV feature, no information from after T.

**Done when:** `run_backtest` can return candidate/positive counts per cutoff, and a unit test covers the leakage rule on a mini dataset.

**Depends on:** P1-3

issues.title: [P2-4] Backtest metrics, chart and honest write-up
issues.body:
For each cutoff compare `cvss_only`, `epss_only`, `blend` (0.35/0.30 reweighted to 1), `cvss>=7`, `cvss>=9`. Metric: share of positives caught when patching the top 5% and 10% of candidates (threshold rules: report fraction patched + fraction caught).
Outputs: `docs/backtest.png`, `docs/backtest_results.csv`, and `docs/backtest.md` (3-5 lines: method, result, limitations, incl. "KEV and asset factors are context and not testable here"). One command: `python -m patchpilot.backtest`.
If the blend does not beat EPSS-only, say so plainly: "matches EPSS, adds asset context and fixes".

**Done when:** chart + table regenerate with one command and P4 can embed `docs/backtest.png` in the app/deck.

**Depends on:** P2-3

issues.title: [P3-1] Evidence retrieval from SQL + FTS5
issues.body:
Implement `assistant.retrieve(conn, question) -> list[Evidence]`. Rule-based intent routing (regex for CVE ids; keywords: "patch first/priority/top", "why", "fix/patch for", "KEV", "my assets/servers/affected"). Build evidence with ids `CVE-ID:kind` where kind in `score | kev | epss | fix | desc | asset | cwe`:
- Priority questions: top N from `scoring.ranked_queue`, each with `score` evidence (include `scoring.explain` factor text) and `kev` if applicable.
- Fix questions: `fix` rows; if none exist, emit a `fix` evidence saying "no fix link recorded" (so the answer can say so, never invent one).
- Multi-hop ("which of my assets have KEV CVEs with a fix"): SQL join over `asset`/`cve_product`/`kev`/`fix`.
- Fallback: FTS5 over `cve_fts` (sanitise the query for FTS syntax).
- Unknown CVE / out-of-scope question => empty list.

**Done when:** retrieval returns sensible evidence for the 8 starter questions in `data/eval/questions.json` on the fixture.

Contract: `config/project.json`. Edit only files you own. Keep `python -m pytest -q` green.

issues.title: [P3-2] LLM generation: strict JSON, injection-safe, cached
issues.body:
Create `patchpilot/llm.py` (ONE provider, delete the other from `requirements.txt`) and finish `assistant.answer`:
- System prompt: answer ONLY from the evidence; cite evidence ids; if the evidence is insufficient, set `refused=true`.
- Output strict JSON `{answer, citations, refused}`; parse defensively (strip code fences, one retry).
- Wrap evidence in clear delimiters and state that evidence text is untrusted data, never instructions.
- Run `verify_citations`; on failure retry once, then refuse.
- Cache answers by (question, evidence hash) in `data/cache/answers.json` so demo questions never depend on the network.

**Done when:** `answer("What should we patch first?")` returns a cited, verified answer on the fixture; `answer` never raises.

**Depends on:** P3-1

issues.body:

Add `tests/test_verifier.py` with at least 8 cases (good, wrong id, hallucinated CVE, hallucinated URL, wrong score, empty citations, refused-with-citations, injection echo).

**Done when:** all verifier tests green.

issues.title: [P3-4] Eval set (~30 Q) + metrics
issues.body:
Expand `data/eval/questions.json` to ~30 questions (about 10 unanswerable, a few multi-hop, a few "no fix exists", one injection). Implement `eval.run_eval()` -> `{citation_accuracy, refusal_accuracy, n}` and write `docs/eval.md` with the numbers and 3 example failures. Citation accuracy = answered questions where `verify_citations` passes AND `must_cite` CVEs appear. Refusal accuracy = refused iff `expect_refusal`.
Run it on the real snapshot once P1-4 lands (adjust CVE ids in the questions; fixture ids are synthetic).

**Done when:** `python -m patchpilot.eval` prints both numbers; P4 shows them in the app/deck.

**Depends on:** P3-2, P3-3

issues.title: [P4-2] Assets tab: CSV import + RapidFuzz match + review
issues.body:
Implement `assets.import_assets_csv` and `assets.match_asset` (RapidFuzz `WRatio` over distinct `cve_product` "vendor product" strings). CSV columns `name, criticality`; see `data/fixture/sample_assets.csv`. Store `match_confidence`. Confidence >= 0.85 auto-accepted; 0.60-0.85 flagged "needs review"; below 0.60 unmatched.
UI: `st.data_editor` so the user can fix vendor/product on low-confidence rows and save; the queue re-ranks immediately.
No LLM, no embeddings.
